BURHAN:v2p129/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p129/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURHAN:v2p129/r2.claim: The Prophet supported his descriptions of Paradise with verses: unseen delights by 32:17, the promise to work by the verses of al-Layl, and the tree's long shade by 56:30.
BURHAN:v2p129/r2.anchor: منها حين ذكر ما أعد الله تعالى لأوليائه فى الجنة فقال فيها ما لا عين رأت ولا أذن سمعت ولا خطر

QASHANI:92:8-12/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:92:8-12/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:92:8-12/r2.claim: Denying the highest good means rejecting perfection because worldly life suffices for the person and veils the unseen and afterlife.
QASHANI:92:8-12/r2.anchor: بوجود مرتبة الكمال والفضيلة لاستغنائه بالحياة الدنيا

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r5.claim: Verses 8–10 describe the character and belief that lead a person to doom and Hell.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r5.anchor: Mentioned in these verses are the character and ideology of a person which lead him to doom and to the pit of Hell.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p348/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p348/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p348/r5.claim: Those who treat worldly life as ultimate are miserly, heedless of the Hereafter, and lack resolve for its reward; God lets them pursue their chosen way toward hardship.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p348/r5.anchor: They are misers and callously guard their wealth and have no fear of the Hereafter

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p349/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p349/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p349/r1.claim: God leaves people without courage for virtue to their base desires; they may seem to progress smoothly until death, then face the steep hardship of 74:17.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p349/r1.anchor: they reach the end of their lives

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r2.claim: The surah explains which traits bring the success and failure just mentioned in the previous surah, then warns of the Fire and distinguishes those entering it from those spared.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r2.anchor: ولما ذكر فيما قبلها قد أفلح من زكاها وقد خاب من دساها ، ذكر هنا

FARRA:v3p270/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p270/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p270/r6.claim: To deny the good promise is to deny the reward of Paradise, claiming there is no reward.
FARRA:v3p270/r6.anchor: وقوله عز وجل: وكذب بالحسنى (9) : بثواب الجنة: أنه لا ثواب.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p531#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p531#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p531#4/r1.claim: Denying al-ḥusnā means denying Paradise and its reward.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#2/r1.claim: The meaning of al-husna is the same as the interpretations already given for 92:6, here contrasted with believing in it.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#2/r1.anchor: والمراد بالحسنى فيه ما مر في الأقوال قبل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p446/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p446/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p446/r2.claim: The miser withholds good spending, seeks no reward from God, and denies the promised good; God prepares him for evil until he merits the Fire.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p446/r2.anchor: {وكذب بالحسنى فسنيسره للعسرى} سنهيئه للشر بأن نجريه على يديه حتى يعمل بما لا يرضي الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447/r2.claim: In this story, the giver is Abu al-Dahdah, the promised good is reward, and the easier path is Paradise; the miser is the Ansari, who denies reward and is eased toward Hell.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447/r2.anchor: {وأما من بخل واستغنى} يعني الأنصاري، {وكذب بالحسنى} يعني الثواب، {فسنيسره للعسرى} يعني النار.

BAYDAWI-FULL:92:8-12/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:8-12/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:8-12/r2.claim: He denies the good promise and what it signifies.

BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.claim: The oath's night, daylight, and creation frame divergent earthly endeavors, then contrasting afterlife fates: the denier's fire and the pious giver's satisfaction.
BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.anchor: وعلى هذا النسق من البيان المعجز، يتم الربط بين المقسم به في أول السورة:

BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r5.claim: The miser denies al-ḥusnā, rejecting that it deserves to be believed.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r5.anchor: أي أوقع التكذيب أن يستحق التصديق

DURR-FULL:v8p534/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r5.claim: He reports that Abu Bakr bought and freed Bilal for God; the verses contrast their efforts with those of Umayya and Ubayy, identify the good as the testimony of faith, and the hard path as Hell.
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r5.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم وأبو الشيخ وابن عساكر عن ابن مسعود

DURR-FULL:v8p534/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r6.speaker: ابن عباس عن عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r6.claim: Giving means giving from one's bounty and fearing God; the good promise is God's compensation, ease is good, and the opposite is withholding wealth, self-sufficiency, denial, and ease toward evil.
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r6.anchor: وأخرج سعيد بن منصور وعبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم وابن جرير والبيهقي في شعب الإيمان من طريق عكرمة عن ابن عباس

DURR-FULL:v8p534/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r7.claim: He said the giver pays God's due, avoids prohibitions, and believes God's promise; the miser withholds that due, feels self-sufficient, and denies the promise.
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r7.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن أبي حاتم عن قتادة

DURR-FULL:v8p535/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r4.speaker: ابن عباس عن أبي صالح
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r4.claim: In a report through al-Kalbi and Abu Salih, the giver and God-fearing person is Abu Bakr, while the miser who feels self-sufficient and denies the good is Abu Sufyan ibn Harb.
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r4.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن مردويه وابن عساكر في طريق الكلبي عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس

DURR-FULL:v8p535/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r5.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r5.claim: The Prophet said each person's place in Paradise or Fire is written, but commanded people to act: each is made ready for the deeds of the saved or the wretched, then recited this passage.
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r5.anchor: وأخرج أحمد وعبد بن حميد والبخاري ومسلم وأبو داود والترمذي والنسائي وابن ماجة وابن مردويه وابن جرير عن علي بن أبي طالب

DURR-FULL:v8p537/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r2.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r2.claim: Suraqa asked whether deeds were predetermined; the Prophet affirmed the decree but urged action, since each person is eased toward what he was created for, then recited the passage.
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r2.anchor: وأخرج أحمد ومسلم وابن حبان والطبراني وابن مردويه عن جابر بن عبد الله

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3439/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3439/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3439/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas links the sura's revelation to a sale: a stingy palm owner deprived a poor household of fallen dates, then a believer traded forty palms for the tree and gave it to the family; the buyer received a promised palm in Paradise.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3439/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس : ان رجلا كان له نخل ومنها نخلة فرعها إلى دار رجل صالح فقير ذي عيال

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the miser withholds wealth, relies on himself, denies God's replacement, and is eased toward evil.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r2.anchor: واما من بخل واستغنى قال : بخل بماله واستغنى عن ربه وكذب بالحسنى قال : الخلف من الله فسنيسره للعسرى قال : للشر من الله

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r6.claim: Qatadah says denying the good means disbelieving God's promise.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r6.anchor: وكذب الحسنى قال : بموعود الله الذي وعد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p382/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p382/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p382/r4.claim: الحسنى is a feminine form of الأفضل with an implied feminine noun such as reward, victory, promise, or outcome; it can also conventionally denote Paradise, the testimony of faith, prayer, or alms. Believing in God's good promise entails hoping for it and doing deeds to attain it, hence the opposite denial.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p382/r4.anchor: والحسنى : تأنيث الأحسن فهي بالأصالة صفة لموصوف مقدر ، وتأنيثها مشعر بأن موصوفها المقدر يعتبر مؤنث اللفظ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r3.claim: The passage uses الجمع مع التقسيم and four antitheses: giving versus withholding, piety versus self-sufficiency, affirmation versus denial, and ease versus hardship.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p150#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p150#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p150#2/r1.claim: The explanations of al-ḥusnā were given earlier at 92:6.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417#2/r4.claim: Here the good promise means recompense in the next life, which the miserly person denies.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417#2/r4.anchor: وكذب بالحسنى} أي: بالجزاء في الدار الآخرة.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p767/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p767/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p767/r3.claim: One report says these verses concern Abu Bakr and Abu Sufyan ibn Harb.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p767/r3.anchor: وقيل : نزلتا في أبي بكر رضي الله عنه ، وفي أبي سفيان بن حرب

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r34.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r34.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r34.claim: Mawardi says the same seven interpretations of al-husna listed for the preceding verse apply to what this person denies.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r38.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r38.speaker: أبو الدرداء
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r38.claim: Qatada reports from Khulayd, from Abu al-Darda, that the Prophet said two angels call each sunrise for God to replace the spender's gift and ruin the hoarder's wealth, then recited these verses; no grading is stated.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r38.anchor: يروي قتادة عن خليد عن أبي الدرداء أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( ما من يوم طلعت فيه شمسه إلا وملكان يناديان : اللهم

QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r1.speaker: علي عن النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r1.claim: At a funeral in Baqiʿ, the Prophet says each soul's destination is written, but people must act; each person is made ready for the work of the blessed or wretched, then he recites these verses.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r1.anchor: ما من نفس منفوسة إلا قد كتب مدخلها

QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r2.speaker: علي عن النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r2.claim: Al-Tirmidhi's wording is graded hasan sahih; the Prophet repeats that everyone is made easy for the work for which they were created.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r2.anchor: بل اعملوا فكل ميسر أما من كان من أهل السعادة فإنه ييسر لعمل السعادة

QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r3.speaker: غلامان شابان عن النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r3.claim: Two young men ask whether deeds follow prior decrees or begin anew; the Prophet says decrees, then tells them to act because each is enabled for the work assigned to him.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r3.anchor: «بل فيما جفت به الأقلام، وجرت به المقادير» قالا: ففيم العمل

QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r4.speaker: الغلامان
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r4.claim: After hearing that each is made easy for the work for which he was created, the young men say they will strive and work.

QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r9.claim: Denying al-ḥusnā means denying God's compensation; Mujahid alternatively says it means denying Paradise or the testimony of monotheism.

QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r10.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r10.claim: In two reports, he glosses al-ḥusnā as Paradise and as the declaration that there is no god but God.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r10.anchor: وروى ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد: «وكذب بالحسنى» قال: بالجنة. وبإسناد عنه آخر قال: «بالحسنى» أي بلا إله إلا الله.

QUTB-ZILAL:92:9/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:92:9/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:92:9/r1.claim: The one who denies al-husna rejects the good creed and God’s call and religion, joining the rank that withholds and claims independence.
QUTB-ZILAL:92:9/r1.anchor: ومن بخل بنفسه وماله . واستغنى عن الله وهداه . وكذب بهذه الحسنى

QUTB-ZILAL:92:9/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:92:9/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:92:9/r2.claim: The many kinds of people, efforts, methods, and aims converge in two broad ranks, each with its own path and facilitation.
QUTB-ZILAL:92:9/r2.anchor: هذان هما الصفان اللذان يلتقي فيهما شتات النفوس ، وشتات السعي

QUTB-ZILAL:92:9/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:92:9/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:92:9/r3.claim: A person who withholds self and wealth and denies God’s call and religion carries self toward the greatest possible corruption.
QUTB-ZILAL:92:9/r3.anchor: يبلغ أقصى ما يبلغه إنسان بنفسه من تعريضها للفساد

RAZI-FULL:v31p180#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#2/r1.claim: The passage explains that the differing human paths end in praiseworthy or blameworthy outcomes, reward or punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#2/r1.anchor: بين معنى اختلاف الأعمال فيما قلناه من العاقبة المحمودة والمذمومة

STUDYQURAN:92:5/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r1.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r1.claim: ʿAlī reports that the Prophet taught each person's destination is recorded, then urged action because everyone is eased toward what they were created for; he recited these verses.
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r1.anchor: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib related that the Prophet said, “There is no one among you except that his place is registered

STUDYQURAN:92:5/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r4.speaker: most
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r4.claim: Most take al-ḥusnā as the testimony that there is no god but God; another gloss is belief in God, either of which is attested to or denied.
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r4.anchor: is taken by most to mean “There is no god but God” (Sh) or simply belief in God (Z)

STUDYQURAN:92:5/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r5.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r5.claim: Others understand al-ḥusnā as Paradise, called the most beautiful reward in 3:148 and 3:195.
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r5.anchor: others see it as a reference to Paradise, which is referred to as the most beautiful reward in 3:148 and 3:195

STUDYQURAN:92:5/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r6.claim: Al-ḥusnā can also refer to God Himself, whose Most Beautiful Names are affirmed in several verses.
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r6.anchor: it can also be seen as a reference to God Himself, for, as several verses attest, Unto Him belong the Most Beautiful Names

STUDYQURAN:92:5/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r10.claim: Al-ḥusnā can mean the Garden's reward, the Garden's reality, God's Reality, or all three; the discussion also applies to 92:6.
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r10.anchor: What is most beautiful here can mean the reward of the Garden, the reality of the Garden itself, the Reality of God, or all three

TAB-FULL:v24p468/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p468/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p468/r1.claim: He takes denial of al-husna to mean denying God's promised replacement, while reporting other interpretations parallel to those for the corresponding positive phrase.
TAB-FULL:v24p468/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {وكذب بالحسنى} [الليل: 9] وكذب بالخلف

TAB-FULL:v24p468/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p468/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p468/r2.claim: They say the denier rejects God's promised replacement or good promise.
TAB-FULL:v24p468/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، {وكذب بالحسنى} [الليل: 9] وكذب بموعود الله الذي وعد

TAB-FULL:v24p468/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p468/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v24p468/r3.claim: Another interpretation says he denies God's oneness and the testimony that there is no deity but God.
TAB-FULL:v24p468/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {وكذب بالحسنى} [الليل: 9] وكذب بلا إله إلا الله

TAB-FULL:v24p468/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p468/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p468/r4.claim: Mujahid understands the denied al-husna as Paradise.

TAB-FULL:v24p470/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p470/r3.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن علي
TAB-FULL:v24p470/r3.claim: When asked whether people should rely on their written destinies, the Prophet commands them to act: each person is made ready for his path, and he recites the two contrasting passages.

TAB-FULL:v24p471/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r1.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن علي
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r1.claim: Several versions say each person's place in Paradise or Hell is written, yet people must act; each is facilitated toward the work for which they were created.
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r1.anchor: لا اعملوا فكل ميسر لما خلق له

TAB-FULL:v24p471/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r2.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن النزال بن سبرة
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r2.claim: A report says every soul's outcome is written; in response to an Arab's question the Prophet says God guides each person toward good or evil, with these verses cited.
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r2.anchor: كل ميسر لما خلق له، فمن يرد الله به خيرا

TAB-FULL:v24p471/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r3.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن سعد بن عبيدة وأبي عبد الرحمن السلمي
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r3.claim: When asked what work means if everything is decreed, the Prophet says to act because each person is facilitated for the easier or harder path.
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r3.anchor: اعملوا فكل ميسر: سنيسره لليسرى، وسنيسره للعسرى

TAB-FULL:v24p473/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p473/r2.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن جابر بن عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v24p473/r2.claim: Asked whether people act for something already decided or begin something new, the Prophet answers that every worker is made ready for his work.

TAB-FULL:v24p473/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p473/r3.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن بشير بن كعب
TAB-FULL:v24p473/r3.claim: The Prophet says work follows what the pens and decrees have fixed, but people must still act; each is facilitated for the work for which they were created.
TAB-FULL:v24p473/r3.anchor: اعملوا، فكل عامل ميسر لعمله الذي خلق له

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:7-10:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:7-10:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:7-10:anmerkung/r1.claim: The opposition between ease and hardship parallels 94:5–6, while the promise in 87:8 addresses the messenger.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:7-10:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Vgl. die Entgegensetzung von ʿusr und yusr in 94:5.6 sowie die wie 94:5.6 an den Verkünder gerichtete Verheißung 87:8

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:9:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:9:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:9:anmerkung/r1.claim: The commentary compares the uses of kaḏḏaba at 92:16, 95:7, and 73:11, and refers back to its note on al-ḥusnā in verse 6.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:9:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Zu den verschiedenen Gebrauchsweisen von kaḏḏaba s. u. die Anmerkungen zu V. 16 sowie die Anmerkungen zu 95:7 und 73:11

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.claim: The sura develops two antitheses: behavior and recompense for the saved and damned, first in verses 5–13 and then in verses 14–21.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.anchor: Es folgen zwei Antithesen (V. 5–13 und V. 14–21), welche die Verhaltensweisen und Jenseitsschicksale von Seligen und Verdammten miteinander kontrastieren

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r2.claim: The first antithesis pairs virtue and vice catalogues with promises of their eschatological outcomes; first-person plural marks these promises as God's speech and authorizes them alongside the oath.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r2.anchor: Diese Ankündigungen stehen in der ersten Person Plural, sind also eindeutig als Gottesrede markiert – ein Mittel literarischer Autorisierung

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r4.claim: The first stanza is symmetrical, with matching behavior-to-consequence sequences and a cross-rhyme produced by vowel variation, as Neuwirth observes.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r4.anchor: Die symmetrische Binnengliederung des Gesätzes in eine zweimalige Durchführung des Schemas ‚diesseitiges Verhalten – jenseitige Konsequenz’ unterstreicht ein durch Vokalvariation erzielter Kreuzreimeffekt

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r5.claim: The two halves are linked by paired terms: giving versus stinginess, piety versus self-sufficiency, affirmation versus denial, and ease versus hardship.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r5.anchor: V. 5 und 8 sind durch die Verwendung von Antonymen aufeinander bezogen: ʾaʿtā, „geben“ vs. baḫila, „geizen“, ittaqā, „gottesfürchtig sein“ vs. istaġnā

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r6.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r6.speaker: Neuwirth
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r6.claim: Neuwirth classifies verse 11 with the theological predication in verses 12–13 rather than with the preceding description of the wicked.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r6.anchor: anders Neuwirth, Studien, 229 und Neuwirth, Frühmekkanische Suren, 228

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.claim: The final stanza reverses the earlier order of saved and damned; the outer blessed sections are linked by ittaqā in verse 5 and ʾatqā in verse 17.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.anchor: Zum einen wird die Reihenfolge Seliger – Verdammter (V. 5–7 und V. 8–11) jetzt invertiert (V. 14–16 Verdammter, V. 17–20 Seliger)

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.claim: The stanza halves mirror one another: earlier behavior lists precede reward or warning, while the final warning and promise precede each group's worldly conduct.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.anchor: In V. 5–7 und V. 8–11 ging zunächst ein Tugend- bzw. Lasterkatalog voraus, auf den dann jeweils ein Drohwort bzw. eine Verheißung folgten

THALABI:v10p217/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p217/r1.speaker: أبو الدرداء عن النبي
THALABI:v10p217/r1.claim: At each sunset two angels call out for all creatures except humans and jinn: God should repay the spender and destroy the hoarder; the passage was revealed about this contrast.
THALABI:v10p217/r1.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ما من يوم غربت شمسه إلا

THALABI:v10p217/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p217/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p217/r7.claim: The miser withholds good spending, acts as if independent of God and denies the promised good; God then turns him toward disapproved deeds and punishment, with al-ʿusrā also understood as Hell itself.
THALABI:v10p217/r7.anchor: وأما من بخل بالنفقة في الخير واستغنى عن ربه فلم يرغب في ثوابه وكذب بالحسنى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p81/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p81/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p81/r1.claim: He denies the al-husna that Abu Bakr affirmed; its meaning was explained earlier.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p81/r1.anchor: {وكذب بالحسنى} يعني بما صدق (به) (¬4) أبو بكر وقد فسرنا (¬5)

ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r7.claim: Denying al-husnā means rejecting the better reward and outcome for those who do good and adopting pessimism that giving and restraint have no benefit.
ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r7.anchor: “gün günden beterdir, ihsânın korunmanın fâidesi yoktur” diyerek âkıbet hakkında bedbin olmuş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.claim: Others say verses 5–19 were revealed about Abu Bakr; regardless of a specific occasion, the message and rulings are general.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.anchor: bazıları ise 5-19. âyetlerin (bk. Elmalılı, VIII, 5881), müşriklerin işkence ettiği köleleri satın alıp âzat ederek hürriyetlerine kavuşturan Hz. Ebû Bekir hakkında indiğini söylemişlerdir. Âyetler böyle bir özel olay üzerine gelmiş olsa da, hükümleri ve mesajları geneldir

QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.claim: An alternative contextual account identifies the giver as Abu al-Dahdah and the miser as the Ansari palm owner; it maps ease to Paradise, hardship to Hell, and death to loss of wealth.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.anchor: { فأما من أعطى واتقى } يعني أبا الدحداح. { وصدق بالحسنى } أي بالثواب

THALABI:v10p220/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p220/r1.speaker: عطاء
THALABI:v10p220/r1.claim: A man refused the Prophet’s offer of a date palm in Paradise for his palm that dropped fruit into a neighbor’s yard; Abū al-Daḥdāḥ bought and donated it, and the Prophet transferred it to the neighbor. The account identifies them with the surah’s contrasting figures.
THALABI:v10p220/r1.anchor: عطاء قال: كان لرجل من الأنصار نخلة، وكان له جار، فكان يسقط من بلحها في دار جاره

THALABI:v10p220/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p220/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p220/r3.claim: The palm’s owner represents the miser who deems himself self-sufficient and denies reward; he is eased toward Hell and is the “most wretched” who enters the blazing fire.
THALABI:v10p220/r3.anchor: وأما من بخل واستغنى يعني الأنصاري وكذب بالحسنى يعني الثواب فسنيسره للعسرى يعني النار

TAB:92:9/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:9/r1.speaker: author
TAB:92:9/r1.claim: Al-Tabari prefers ‘denied the recompense’ as the meaning of denying al-husna.
TAB:92:9/r1.anchor: وأما نحن فنقول :  معناه :  وكذب بالخلف

TAB:92:9/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:9/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:92:9/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses al-husna as the recompense from God.
TAB:92:9/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس وَكَذّبَ بالحسنى بالخلف من الله

TAB:92:9/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:9/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB:92:9/r3.claim: Qatada says the disbeliever denied God's promise, the good promise He made.
TAB:92:9/r3.anchor: عن قتادة وكذب بالحسنى وكذب بموعود الله الذي وعد

TAB:92:9/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:9/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB:92:9/r4.claim: In another report, Qatada says the disbeliever denied God's good promise.
TAB:92:9/r4.anchor: عن قتادة وكذب بالحسنى وكذب الكافر بموعود الله الحسن

TAB:92:9/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:9/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:92:9/r5.claim: Another interpretation from Ibn Abbas is that al-husna means the profession ‘There is no god but God.’
TAB:92:9/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس وَكَذّبَ بالحسنى :  وكذب بلا إله إلا الله

TAB:92:9/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:9/r6.speaker: الضحاك
TAB:92:9/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak likewise glosses al-husna as ‘There is no god but God.’
TAB:92:9/r6.anchor: سمعت الضحاك يقول في قوله :  وكذب بالحسنى بلا إله إلا الله

TAB:92:9/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:9/r7.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:92:9/r7.claim: Mujahid gives another view: al-husna is Paradise.
TAB:92:9/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد وكذب بالحسنى قال :  بالجنة

ALUSI:92:9/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:9/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:9/r1.claim: The object of denial, al-ḥusnā, has the interpretations already discussed for verse 6.
ALUSI:92:9/r1.anchor: والمراد بالحسنى فيه ما مر في الأقوال قبل

ALUSI:92:9/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:9/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:9/r2.claim: The contrast describes withholding wealth from good, disdain for God's provision or preference for worldly pleasure, and denial of al-ḥusnā; the alternative gloss of withholding commanded acts is dismissed.
ALUSI:92:9/r2.anchor: بما له فلم يبذله في سبيل الخير وقيل أي بخل بفعل ما أمر به وفيه ما فيه

ALUSI:92:10/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:10/r5.speaker: الإرشاد
ALUSI:92:10/r5.claim: Al-Irshād says giving and withholding head the two clauses, though lower in rank than what follows, because each is foundational to the ensuing faith and piety or denial and self-sufficiency.
ALUSI:92:10/r5.anchor: لعل تصدير القسمين بالإعطاء والبخل مع أن كلا منهما أدنى رتبة مما بعد

BAGHAWI:92:10/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:10/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:92:10/r1.claim: God prepares the denier for evil, letting him perform what displeases God until he deserves the Fire.
BAGHAWI:92:10/r1.anchor: سنهيئه للشر بأن نجريه على يديه حتى يعمل بما لا يرضي الله ،   فيستوجب به النار

BAGHAWI:92:10/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:10/r4.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI:92:10/r4.claim: An anonymous report says the passage was revealed about Abu Bakr buying Bilal from Umayya ibn Khalaf for a garment and ten coins and freeing him; their opposed efforts are contrasted.
BAGHAWI:92:10/r4.anchor: قيل : نزلت في أبي بكر الصديق اشترى بلالاً من أمية ابن خلف ببردة وعشرة أوراق ،   فأعتقه

BAGHAWI:92:10/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:10/r5.speaker: عطاء
BAGHAWI:92:10/r5.claim: Ata recounts an Ansari's palm tree whose fallen dates entered a neighbor's home; the Prophet offered a tree in Paradise, the owner refused, and Abu al-Dahdah bought it with his garden and gave it to the neighbor. The report maps the giver to Abu al-Dahdah and the miser to the Ansari.
BAGHAWI:92:10/r5.anchor: عن عطاء ،   قال : " كان لرجل من الأنصار نخلة وكان له جار يسقط من بلحها في داره

BAYDAWI:92:9/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:92:9/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:92:9/r1.claim: He denies al-ḥusnā and rejects what it signifies.

BIQAI:92:9/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:9/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:92:9/r1.claim: He denies al-ḥusnā, bringing about denial of what deserves to be affirmed and believed.
BIQAI:92:9/r1.anchor: أي أوقع التكذيب أن يستحق التصديق

DURR:92:5/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:5/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:92:5/r4.claim: In the report through ʿIkrima, Ibn Abbas says the miser denies God's recompense and God makes him easy for evil.
DURR:92:5/r4.anchor: من طريق عكرمة عن ابن عباس في قوله : { فأما من أعطى } من الفضل { واتقى } قال : اتقى ربه

DURR:92:5/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:5/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR:92:5/r6.claim: Qatada says the miser withholds God's due, feels independent of his Lord, and denies God's promised reward.
DURR:92:5/r6.anchor: عن قتادة { فأما من أعطى } قال : أعطى حق الله عليه { واتقى } محارم الله

DURR:92:5/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:5/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:92:5/r13.claim: In a report through al-Kalbi and Abu Salih, Ibn Abbas identifies the giver as Abu Bakr and the miser who denies the good as Abu Sufyan ibn Harb.
DURR:92:5/r13.anchor: في طريق الكلبي عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس في قوله : { فأما من أعطى واتقى وصدق بالحسنى فسنيسره لليسرى } قال : أبو بكر الصديق

DURR:92:5/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:5/r14.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR:92:5/r14.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet said each person's place in Paradise and Hell is written, yet commanded action: people are facilitated toward deeds of felicity or misery, then he recited these verses.
DURR:92:5/r14.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب قال : «كنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في جنازة فقال : ما منكم من أحد إلا وقد كتب مقعده من الجنة ومقعده من النار

DURR:92:5/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:5/r15.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
DURR:92:5/r15.claim: Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami reports that after 54:49 was revealed, a man asked whether deeds were newly begun or already decreed; the Prophet replied to act, since each is facilitated toward ease or hardship.
DURR:92:5/r15.anchor: عن أبي عبد الرحمن السلمي قال : لما نزلت هذه الآية { إنا كل شيء خلقناه بقدر } [ القمر : 49 ] قال رجل : يا رسول الله ففيم العمل

DURR:92:6/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:6/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:92:6/r4.claim: In the report through ʿIkrima, Ibn Abbas says the miser denies God's recompense and God makes him easy for evil.
DURR:92:6/r4.anchor: من طريق عكرمة عن ابن عباس في قوله : { فأما من أعطى } من الفضل { واتقى } قال : اتقى ربه

DURR:92:6/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:6/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR:92:6/r6.claim: Qatada says the miser withholds God's due, feels independent of his Lord, and denies God's promised reward.
DURR:92:6/r6.anchor: عن قتادة { فأما من أعطى } قال : أعطى حق الله عليه { واتقى } محارم الله

DURR:92:6/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:6/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:92:6/r13.claim: In a report through al-Kalbi and Abu Salih, Ibn Abbas identifies the giver as Abu Bakr and the miser who denies the good as Abu Sufyan ibn Harb.
DURR:92:6/r13.anchor: في طريق الكلبي عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس في قوله : { فأما من أعطى واتقى وصدق بالحسنى فسنيسره لليسرى } قال : أبو بكر الصديق

DURR:92:6/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:6/r14.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR:92:6/r14.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet said each person's place in Paradise and Hell is written, yet commanded action: people are facilitated toward deeds of felicity or misery, then he recited these verses.
DURR:92:6/r14.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب قال : «كنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في جنازة فقال : ما منكم من أحد إلا وقد كتب مقعده من الجنة ومقعده من النار

DURR:92:6/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:6/r15.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
DURR:92:6/r15.claim: Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami reports that after 54:49 was revealed, a man asked whether deeds were newly begun or already decreed; the Prophet replied to act, since each is facilitated toward ease or hardship.
DURR:92:6/r15.anchor: عن أبي عبد الرحمن السلمي قال : لما نزلت هذه الآية { إنا كل شيء خلقناه بقدر } [ القمر : 49 ] قال رجل : يا رسول الله ففيم العمل

DURR:92:7/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:7/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:92:7/r4.claim: In the report through ʿIkrima, Ibn Abbas says the miser denies God's recompense and God makes him easy for evil.
DURR:92:7/r4.anchor: من طريق عكرمة عن ابن عباس في قوله : { فأما من أعطى } من الفضل { واتقى } قال : اتقى ربه

DURR:92:7/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:7/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR:92:7/r6.claim: Qatada says the miser withholds God's due, feels independent of his Lord, and denies God's promised reward.
DURR:92:7/r6.anchor: عن قتادة { فأما من أعطى } قال : أعطى حق الله عليه { واتقى } محارم الله

DURR:92:7/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:7/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:92:7/r13.claim: In a report through al-Kalbi and Abu Salih, Ibn Abbas identifies the giver as Abu Bakr and the miser who denies the good as Abu Sufyan ibn Harb.
DURR:92:7/r13.anchor: في طريق الكلبي عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس في قوله : { فأما من أعطى واتقى وصدق بالحسنى فسنيسره لليسرى } قال : أبو بكر الصديق

DURR:92:7/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:7/r14.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب

DURR:92:7/r14.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب قال : «كنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في جنازة فقال : ما منكم من أحد إلا وقد كتب مقعده من الجنة ومقعده من النار

DURR:92:8/r13.speaker: ابن عباس

DURR:92:8/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:8/r15.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
DURR:92:8/r15.claim: Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami reports that after 54:49 was revealed, a man asked whether deeds were newly begun or already decreed; the Prophet replied to act, since each is facilitated toward ease or hardship.
DURR:92:8/r15.anchor: عن أبي عبد الرحمن السلمي قال : لما نزلت هذه الآية { إنا كل شيء خلقناه بقدر } [ القمر : 49 ] قال رجل : يا رسول الله ففيم العمل

IBNASHUR:92:5/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:5/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:5/r6.claim: The two main groups may be those enabled toward ease and those toward hardship, encompassing different deeds and serving exhortation and warning.
IBNASHUR:92:5/r6.anchor: فريق ميسر لليسرى وفريق ميسر للعسرى

IBNASHUR:92:5/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:5/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:5/r7.claim: The division is also illustrated by the day people emerge separately to see their deeds, including outcomes of even the smallest good or evil.
IBNASHUR:92:5/r7.anchor: كقوله تعالى : { يومئذٍ يصدر الناس أشتاتاً ليروا أعمالهم

IBNASHUR:92:5/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:5/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:5/r8.claim: Alternatively, the groups are the two sets of three traits stated in verses 5 and 8–9, a valid division of varied striving.
IBNASHUR:92:5/r8.anchor: واتّقى وصدّق بالحسنى ، ومنْ بخل واستغنى وكذب بالحسنى

IBNASHUR:92:5/r21.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:5/r21.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:5/r21.claim: Together, the three traits characterize a polytheist.
IBNASHUR:92:5/r21.anchor: وهذه الخلال كناية عن كونه من المشركين

IBNHIBBAN:335/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:335/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNHIBBAN:335/r1.claim: ʿAlī reports that the Prophet said each person's place in Paradise or Hell is recorded; when asked whether to rely on this, he said to act, since each is facilitated, then recited al-Layl 92:5–10.
IBNHIBBAN:335/r1.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان في جنازة فأخذ عودا ينكت في الأرض

IBNHIBBAN:v2p47#2/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:v2p47#2/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNHIBBAN:v2p47#2/r1.claim: ʿAlī reports that the Prophet said each person's place in Paradise or Hell is recorded; when asked whether to rely on this, he said to act, since each is facilitated, then recited al-Layl 92:5–10.
IBNHIBBAN:v2p47#2/r1.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان في جنازة فأخذ عودا ينكت في الأرض

IBNHIBBAN:v2p47#2/r2.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:v2p47#2/r2.speaker: شعبة
IBNHIBBAN:v2p47#2/r2.claim: Shuʿba adds that Manṣūr ibn al-Muʿtamir also narrated the report to him, corroborating its transmission from Sulaymān al-Aʿmash.
IBNHIBBAN:v2p47#2/r2.anchor: قال شعبة حدثني منصور بن المعتمر فلم أنكره من حديث سليمان

IBNKATHIR:92:9/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:92:9/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:92:9/r1.claim: Here al-ḥusnā is the recompense in the afterlife.

KASHSHAF:92:10/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:92:10/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:92:10/r4.claim: A report says these verses were revealed concerning Abū Bakr and Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb.
KASHSHAF:92:10/r4.anchor: نزلتا في أبي بكر رضي الله عنه

MAWARDI:92:9/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:9/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI:92:9/r1.claim: Māwardī says the seven interpretations of al-ḥusnā given for the preceding verse also apply here.

NASAFI:92:9/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:92:9/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:92:9/r1.claim: Denying al-ḥusnā means denying Islam or Paradise.

QURTUBI:92:9/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:9/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:92:9/r1.claim: Al-Qurtubi glosses denying the good as denying God's promised recompense for giving.

QURTUBI:92:9/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:9/r2.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI:92:9/r2.claim: Mujahid, in Ibn Abi Najih's transmission, interprets the good as Paradise.
QURTUBI:92:9/r2.anchor: وروى ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد : " وكذب بالحسن " قال : بالجنة

QURTUBI:92:9/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:9/r3.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI:92:9/r3.claim: In another transmission from Mujahid, the good means the testimony that there is no god but God.
QURTUBI:92:9/r3.anchor: وبإسناد عنه آخر قال " بالحسنى " أي بلا إله إلا اللّه

RAZI:92:1/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:1/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:92:1/r2.claim: Despite that reported occasion, the sūra’s meaning is general, as its statements that human striving differs and that a blazing fire is warned of show.
RAZI:92:1/r2.anchor: إلا أنها وإن كانت كذلك لكن معانيها عامة للناس

RAZI:92:5/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:5/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:92:5/r1.claim: The paired descriptions explain how differing deeds lead to good or bad outcomes, reward or punishment.
RAZI:92:5/r1.anchor: ثم إنه سبحانه بين معنى اختلاف الأعمال فيما قلناه من العاقبة المحمودة

RAZI:92:6/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:6/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:92:6/r5.claim: On the replacement interpretation, denying the promise means withholding wealth through a bad opinion of God; a proverb says withholding what one has reflects such mistrust.
RAZI:92:6/r5.anchor: فبخل بماله لسوء ظنه بالمعبود ، كما قال بعضهم : منع الموجود
